reviews.text: Fails to deliver. If you’re after photo preservation, do not download this app. It is unable to restore older photos. I’ve tried images from the 1980s-early 2000s and the results are hardly discernible from the original. You’ll typically notice an adjustment to the exposure and/or saturation but that’s the extent of it. Any so-called retouches to human faces are so ridiculously cartoonish that grandma will suddenly look like she’s has Botox and veneers. The app hallucinates details and makes everyone look like the same person or renders halos and plastic textures. Like I said, if you want your vintage photos to look as though they were taken on a better camera and not by a different person, then steer away from this app.

reviews.text:
Terrible. I paid for a week of Remini AI photos expecting stylized versions of MYSELF, not random AI women wearing toddler roller skates, sitting in strawberry fields, hiding in teddy bears, or looking like Celine Dion’s emotionally unavailable cousin.

The app constantly generated faces, bodies, hair, makeup, and expressions that barely resembled me at all. Every batch looked like the same generic AI influencer template with different costumes pasted on top.

The advertising makes it seem like you upload selfies and get polished cinematic portraits of yourself. What you actually get is uncanny valley stock-photo strangers wearing your skin as a suggestion.

The interface is also terrible. Projects get stuck, photos reload repeatedly, deleting images doesn’t actually clear the generation, and it’s extremely confusing trying to generate new looks versus reopening old ones.

For nine dollars, this was honestly ridiculous. If you want realistic enhancement of actual photos, this app is not it.
